title: Comparisons between relative limit cones
statement:
Use small quasicategories, coherent functor categories, mapping spaces, homotopy fibres and equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], inner fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and relative limit diagrams and joins of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone]. Let $q:D\to B$ be an inner fibration of small quasicategories, let $K$ be a small simplicial set, and let $\lambda,\mu:K^{\triangleleft}\to D$ be $q$-limit diagrams with equal boundaries and equal images in $B$. The homotopy fibre of the mapping-space map
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K^{\triangleleft},D)}(\lambda,\mu)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,D)}(\lambda|_K,\mu|_K)\mathop{\times}^{h}_{\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,B)}(q\lambda|_K,q\mu|_K)}\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K^{\triangleleft},B)}(q\lambda,q\mu)$$
over the pair of identities is contractible. Every coherent comparison in this fibre has an equivalence on cone vertices. In particular, a specified comparison between two relative product cones with identical boundary and base is an equivalence on their apices. This includes an empty boundary.

proof.text: Apply the defining relative-limit square of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone] for the target cone $\mu$, taking the test diagram $t=\lambda$. The limit convention has mapping spaces $\operatorname{Map}(t,\mu)$, so this is exactly the square inducing the displayed map. The equal-boundary and equal-base hypotheses specify its target point as the two identities with the constant path between their common restrictions. By [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] the four corner mapping spaces are Kan. Its path-pullback target is Kan as well: apply [lem-coef-space-path-fibration-replacement] to the upper-right to lower-right map and pull its endpoint fibration back along the lower-left to lower-right map. Pullbacks of Kan fibrations are Kan fibrations directly by the horn lifting definition, and a Kan fibration over a Kan complex has Kan total space by two successive horn lifts. The relative-limit definition says that the canonical map to this path pullback is a weak equivalence. Thus [lem-coef-space-contractible-fiber-equivalence] makes its homotopy fibre at the specified identity point contractible.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.6.19(2), with target cone mu and test cone lambda; path model and fibre criterion expanded using the cited DAG statements. Application: Higher Algebra Theorem 2.3.3.23(1), pp. 267-268.

proof.text: Let $a$ be any point of the identity homotopy fibre, retaining its path data. The reversed application (target $\lambda$, test $\mu$) gives a nonempty contractible reverse fibre; choose $b$ there. Here is why the composite comparisons still carry identity-fibre data. In the composition formula of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], the maps $\theta$ and $\ell$ restrict a family of triangles to its edges. Restriction to $K$ and postcomposition by $q$ commute strictly with these restrictions. The pinch comparison $j$ is natural by [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison]. Thus the same triangle families compute composition in all four corner mapping spaces, compatibly with their square. Whisker the boundary/base paths belonging to $a,b$ by these compositions and concatenate them; their compatibility paths in the lower-right mapping space are whiskered in the same triangle family. The resulting path in the path-pullback target ends at the composite of the identity pairs, identified with the identity pair by the unital homotopies of the composition lemma. It therefore supplies points over $ba$ and $ab$ in the self-comparison identity fibres. Those fibres are contractible by Step 1, applied with both cones equal. They also contain the degenerate identities with constant path data. Projecting paths in these fibres to the original mapping spaces shows $[b][a]=[1_\lambda]$ and $[a][b]=[1_\mu]$. The invertible-component criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] makes the edge underlying $a$ an equivalence in $\operatorname{Fun}(K^{\triangleleft},D)$. The component criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] gives an equivalence at the cone vertex.

source.place: Construction 4.6.8.9, Propositions 4.6.8.11-12 and Remark 4.6.8.14; natural pinch comparison 4.6.5.10. Agent expansion of the relative-product comparison used in Higher Algebra Theorem 2.3.3.23(1), p.268.

proof.text: The relative-product-cone conclusion is the specialization of Step 2 to the indexing simplicial set and boundary defining a relative product. The join and relative-limit definitions in [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone] identify its comparison space and its boundary/base maps with those in the displayed fibre, so the apex map is an equivalence. No nonemptiness of the boundary was used; when $K=\varnothing$, the boundary mapping spaces are terminal points and the same identity-fibre argument applies.
